0d66b77606601aa71bd22569b1ad54f41bdbfd1c.tldr: Four independent clocks track system, content, index, and validity time separately to enable time-aware search behavior.
0d66b77606601aa71bd22569b1ad54f41bdbfd1c.summary: The temporal model uses four distinct time dimensions. System time (birthtime, mtime, git history) answers "when was this changed." Content time (dates inside text, coverage metadata) answers "what was planned when." Index time (last summarized, change history) indicates card staleness. Validity time (status, deletion, deprecation) marks currency. Ranking applies recency decay on system time, filters on content time, and demotes deprecated items unless history is explicitly requested.

decisions: Four independent clocks are stored and never conflated.

30c87a2ccc49a19436af3c47502b6d317207a4b6.tldr: Analysis methodology for benchmark scores using median-per-arm, paired bootstrap resampling, and three-gate gating criteria.

3144a480fbb17a88e584ed41702913bc0f986223.tldr: Worker pool adapts concurrency between 4 and 16, retries with escalation model, and applies exponential backoff for rate limits.
3144a480fbb17a88e584ed41702913bc0f986223.summary: The worker pool starts with concurrency of 4 and increases by 1 after 8 consecutive successes up to a maximum of 16, halving on RateLimited errors. Failed requests retry once with the same model, then once with an escalation model (default sonnet), storing failure reasons. RateLimited errors trigger exponential backoff (1s, 4s, 16s) without counting against retry attempts. Pool-stopping Fatal errors cancel tokens and queued jobs report pool stopped status.

decisions: Concurrency starts at 4 and maxes at 16.
Escalation model defaults to sonnet.
RateLimited errors use exponential backoff: 1s, 4s, 16s.

3ba23336e65688caefef9705872540d8f65308f7.summary: The Summarizer executes rounds of Engine::summarize_pending bounded to 2× pool concurrency, prioritizing recently touched documents first, then smaller ones. 4417c6465cb1b03dc988de88e0a49537f0e60b69.tldr: ADR-0003 specifies one daemon per root with notify-based watching, interprocess sockets, and dual SQLite connections for indexing and summarization.
4417c6465cb1b03dc988de88e0a49537f0e60b69.summary: The architecture uses one daemon per watched root, persisting state in `.markdownattractor/` with no global registry. File watching uses `notify` 8.2 plus a custom debouncer that checks size stability before processing events. IPC relies on `interprocess` 2.4 with Unix domain sockets (or named pipes on Windows) using newline-delimited JSON. The daemon maintains two separate SQLite connections for indexing and summarization tasks to avoid contention.

decisions: One daemon per root with state stored in .markdownattractor/ and no global registry.
File watching uses notify 8.2 with a custom ~100-line debouncer checking size stability.
IPC uses interprocess 2.4 with Unix domain sockets (or named pipes on Windows) and newline-delimited JSON.
Two separate SQLite Engine connections assigned to indexer and summarizer tasks to serialize concurrent writes.

48088aeb350fb01109247611525ed01c3e01201d.tldr: Control channel uses newline-delimited JSON over local socket with bounded requests, 32 concurrent clients, and 10-second write deadlines.
48088aeb350fb01109247611525ed01c3e01201d.summary: The control channel operates via newline-delimited JSON over an interprocess local socket. Request lines are capped at 64 KiB with support for ping, status, stop, pause, resume, index, rescan, and watch commands. The system handles up to 32 concurrent clients, enforces 10-second deadlines on response writes, and uses file locking for exclusivity rather than socket-based locking. Socket and state files use 0600 permissions on Unix.

decisions: Control channel uses newline-delimited JSON over local socket.
Request lines are capped at 64 KiB.

Response writes have 10 second deadline.

481895cad5424af8d47de40e8f69551974a39417.tldr: Scope and maintenance demands prevented adoption work, risking deployment and user adoption success.
481895cad5424af8d47de40e8f69551974a39417.summary: The Codex project bundles many interacting components (watcher, parser, worker pool, validator, reducer, database, embeddings, MCP server, CLI) across five platform targets on a tight four to five week timeline, creating extensive maintenance surfaces before establishing user demand. The plan lacks staffing and post-launch support allocation, leaving minimal capacity to address actual adoption blockers and installation failures. Root causes include unvalidated demand for the differentiator, unproven savings after indexing costs, and inability to convert installation into consistent agent usage.

52a50bf2315ed5af61c0af51eb0362be21dd8635.tldr: The intake process watches for file changes, classifies content types, debounces updates, applies batches, and rescans to keep the index synchronized.
52a50bf2315ed5af61c0af51eb0362be21dd8635.summary: The intake pipeline consists of five stages: a recursive file watcher (using `notify` 8) that captures all filesystem events as hints before initial scan; a classifier that ignores `.markdownattractor/`, `.git/`, and entries in ignore files while categorizing remaining paths; a debouncer that holds markdown paths until quiet for 1 second with stable size, batching structural hints; batch application that processes present paths, then missing paths, detects renames via content hash matching, and adds changed documents to the hot set; and a rescan that reindexes all discovered files and tombstones any not found.

Renames are detected via content hash matching; matching is one-to-one.
Rescan short-circuits unchanged documents via content hash verification.

57b16403c4d4b58cc8efcc97873a77b17675f0f6.tldr: Framework establishes rules for fair benchmark comparisons: frozen configs before runs, quality gates before cost claims, whole-system arms, and audited grading by model panel.
57b16403c4d4b58cc8efcc97873a77b17675f0f6.summary: Benchmark evaluation rules ensure reproducible, fair comparisons across tools and datasets. Key constraints: freeze dataset, prompts, and configs before measurement; report failures as results; require quality thresholds (95% grounding, ≥4.0 score, ≥−0.25 bootstrap CI) before claiming cost savings; use model panel grading (Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT Astra) audited blind; preserve artifacts for reproducibility. Test splits use seed 20260922 (30% dev, 55% test, 15% sealed holdout opened once at version 1.0).
questions_answered: What are the rules for reporting token and cost savings in benchmarks?
How are test datasets split and when is the holdout opened?
How is grounding verified and audited in evaluations?

decisions: Cost savings are only reported when all three criteria hold: bootstrap CI lower bound ≥ −0.25, mean score ≥ 4.0, grounding pass rate ≥ 95%.
Grading is performed by a two-model panel (Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT Astra) independently, with disagreements over one point resolved by mean score.
Failures (errors, timeouts, no answer) are counted as results and never become zero-versus-zero parity.
Public artifacts are committed and preserved; private corpus results are clearly separated and exempt from reproducibility claims.

Understand Anything provides a multi-agent pipeline for code understanding with React dashboard and semantic search, but runs one-shot rather than maintaining a background index.

5eaec8923e4bce8033c984a63afa026c995ee772.tldr: Stopping the daemon cancels token calls, finishes batches, and cleans up pid/socket files.
5eaec8923e4bce8033c984a63afa026c995ee772.summary: The `mda stop` command or SIGTERM signal halts the daemon by canceling the token, which cuts off summarizer calls and leaves sections pending. The indexer finishes its current batch, the socket closes, and cleanup files are removed. The daemon waits up to 15 seconds for the pid file to disappear. Crashes leave behind pid, info, and socket files, which are cleaned on next start.

Next start removes leftover pid, info, and socket files from crashes.

6eeec0bdc7bebbd28632c844cb0ee687777a417d.tldr: T5 is a simulated historical replay on Prisma and Tailwind CSS over 60 days, scoring MDA and three baseline tools on 40 questions about page and section changes, timing, and additions.
6eeec0bdc7bebbd28632c844cb0ee687777a417d.summary: T5 replays two project histories (Prisma and Tailwind CSS) from pinned commits, stepping daily through commits touching corpus paths and recording file mtimes and creation dates at each step. It generates 40 seeded questions in three types—which pages/sections changed between dates (set F1 ≥0.8), when pages/sections were last changed or added (within one day), and which pages were added in a month (set F1)—with ground truth from git. Four arms (git baseline, MDA with time index, QMD at final step, Graphify) answer via structured JSON; 3 runs per question score correctness and effort (tool calls, tokens, cost).

decisions: Only Prisma and Tailwind CSS are replayed; Supabase and GitHub Docs excluded for cost; Supabase added if dry-run under $15.
Each project gets fresh clones fetched to full depth and checked out step by step; pinned checkouts remain untouched.
Steps are daily with at least one commit on corpus paths, taken at the last such commit; the 60-day range ends at the pinned commit's author date.
File mtimes are set to each step's commit author date; created_at is the first step date for files present at range start; answers scored via F1 ≥ 0.8 (which) or within one day (when).

8742df24b6aa38398905b16c9206f6d28bbd05a5.tldr: Complete architecture across three phases: document discovery, section parsing, card generation via deterministic or AI pipeline, storage, embedding, and search via BM25 + vectors with RRF ranking.
8742df24b6aa38398905b16c9206f6d28bbd05a5.summary: The system ingests markdown documents through discovery and parsing, then upsets them into raw FTS index. A pipeline chunks sections, invokes a worker pool with AIMD concurrency (api/local/claude-cli backends), validates results, and stores cards and embeddings. Search combines lexical (bm25) and vector (dot-product) methods ranked by RRF, recency, and filters. The daemon maintains file-watching, debouncing, and synchronization via local IPC sockets with exclusive lock-based concurrency.

decisions: Summaries and vectors are keyed by section hash (blake3), not position; moved sections cost nothing.
Every state file uses mode 0600 and refuses symlinks.
Every store transaction is BEGIN IMMEDIATE with 5 s busy timeout for safe file-level concurrency.
Vectors are L2-normalised and VectorIndex scans by dot product without sqlite-vec.

875a45d4f9f77676e5f3bbeede79b15233373ba7.tldr: Code review identifies 16 security, concurrency, and logic issues in the daemon implementation spanning symlink safety, transaction handling, and file synchronization.
875a45d4f9f77676e5f3bbeede79b15233373ba7.summary: A Codex review of the daemon step (Phase 1) found 16 findings: 5 high-severity issues including symlink traversal, feedback loops, race conditions in socket binding, SQLite busy errors, and index inconsistency; 9 medium-severity issues covering graceful shutdown, authentication, resource bounds, rename detection, and pause logic; and 2 low-severity issues. Fixes proposed include symlink-safe writes, exclusive locking, immediate transactions, and normalization of paths.

decisions: Symlink-safe state directory and file writes are required.
Exclusive per-root process lock must protect socket bind, run, and shutdown.

Cancellation must be represented separately from failure in job status.

92902f07fb70864e8c47842ca72cc2ae20d92aae.tldr: Extended thinking causes 8–12 s latency per section; structured output requires explicit system prompt instruction to work reliably on turn one.
92902f07fb70864e8c47842ca72cc2ae20d92aae.summary: Spike testing revealed that extended thinking, not the model itself, drives latency (8–12 s per section, not the planned 3–6 s). Structured output requires a system prompt instruction forcing tool calls on the first turn; without it, Haiku writes JSON as text and needs reminder turns, doubling tokens and causing ~25% failure rate. The worker retries based on response codes, implements AIMD backoff for rate limits, and validates grounding with normalized quote/dash folding.

decisions: Extended thinking must be disabled (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0) to meet latency targets.
System prompt must explicitly state 'your ONLY action is to call the StructuredOutput tool… Call the tool immediately on your first turn'.
Retry policy: null structured_output → retry once then escalate to Sonnet; error/API issues classified by status code with AIMD backoff for rate limits.
Evidence grounding uses NFKC normalization plus quote/dash folding to validate model output.

9d923b0d36daef90ff3d2037e8f5e93457fc174b.tldr: Pipeline architecture uses section hashing for deduplication, worker pools with configurable backends, and SQLite FTS5 for search indexing.
9d923b0d36daef90ff3d2037e8f5e93457fc174b.summary: The system processes markdown files through a discovery→parse→store→summarize pipeline. Sections are keyed by blake3 hash of normalized text for deduplication and movement resilience. State persists in `.markdownattractor/` with an SQLite schema (v2) containing docs, summaries, sections, and FTS5 indexes. Workers use AIMD concurrency with retries and support multiple backends (API, local, claude-cli). Search combines BM25 on cards and raw sections with RRF ranking and recency filters.

decisions: Summaries are keyed by section hash (blake3), not position, so moved/duplicated sections do not cost API calls.
State persists in .markdownattractor/ directory, which is gitignored at any depth.
Sections are identified by doc_id#index format, where doc_id is first 16 hex of blake3(rel_path).
Worker child processes write stdin and drain stdout+stderr concurrently under timeout.

Read-then-write transactions begin IMMEDIATE to prevent busy timeout upgrade failures.
Stopped runs are distinguished from failed sections; environment failures defer separately.
Exclusivity is enforced via OS file lock, not socket availability.

ed95ea3ebbe9542ab4cc4d68b7d99e2d426a5c77.tldr: Pipeline processes markdown sections with debouncing, hashing, parsing, and parallel validation using adaptive concurrency and token budgets.
ed95ea3ebbe9542ab4cc4d68b7d99e2d426a5c77.summary: The pipeline ingests events through a multi-stage flow: debounce, hash-based skip detection, parsing, and section diffing, then plans chunks for parallel MAP processing with validation, reducing to atomic writes and index updates. Line ranges refresh per-parse while hashes persist, enabling efficient detection of unchanged sections even after insertions.

Read-time freshness check re-hashes sections from disk before returning; stale content enqueues at top priority.

f34c6955455d5270c08eb2ac425cadb251460545.summary: An A/B test compared baseline grep/read tools against an index-augmented pipeline on 12 golden corpus questions. ffd8e105b5db1fa68bc356803114fef3d0f95797.tldr: Search results include section ID, path, heading, line range, token estimate, card TLDR, snippet, score, and match type.
ffd8e105b5db1fa68bc356803114fef3d0f95797.summary: Search hits carry metadata about document sections including identifiers, location information, and scoring details. Each hit includes section_id, relative path, heading path, line boundaries, token estimate, optional card TLDR, a truncated snippet, relevance score, match source (cards/raw/both), and pending/update status. The CLI outputs the exact command to open sections.
